headline: Recommended FY27 CPA budget of $1,344,134, extended deadlines for Gruppe Mural and Solar Now grants, and continued discussion of Girdler House generator funding.
summary: The committee reviewed the Girdler House generator project and agreed to send a list of questions to the applicant before deciding on additional funding. It recommended the FY27 CPA budget, extended grant deadlines for the Gruppe Mural and Solar Now projects, reviewed Independence Park documentation, and approved minutes from June 18, 2026.
decisions: Recommended the draft FY27 CPA budget of $1,344,134, including a State match of $176,560, with reserves and administrative budget as outlined, 5-0.
Extended the grant agreement deadline for the Gruppe Mural project to December 31, 2026, 5-0.
Extended the contract deadline for the Solar Now project to December 31, 2026, 5-0.
Approved the June 18, 2026 meeting minutes as presented, 4-0-1.

decision_evidence.quote: Motion to recommend the draft FY27 CPA budget in the amount of $1,344,134 including the State match of $176,560...Motion carries (5-0).
Motion to extend the grant agreement deadline for the Gruppe Mural to December 31, 2026. Marino seconds. Motion carries (5-0).
Motion to extend the contract deadline for the Solar Now project to December 31, 2026. Ershun seconds. Motion carries (5-0).
Motion to approve the meeting minutes of June 18, 2026, as presented. Marino seconds. Motion carries (4-0-1).

5. CPA Project Updates and Reports – The Committee took up this item at this time. 23 
 b. Girdler House Generator_OOC-3_2024 – Status update or potential closeout 24 
 25 
Beth Oldmixon, City Solicitor, explained when the Girdler House originally applied under 26 
affordable housing, it was not allowed because the Girdler House does not have any affordable 27 
housing restrictions on it. The Girdler House then reapplied as a historic property, and they had 28 
the Historic District review the property and designate it as historic. They were then allowed to 29 
proceed under the preservation of a historic property. This was on the edge of what is allowed 30 
because the ability to preserve a property to support the building envelope and the structure 31 
cannot be for the comfort of the people inside the building. There was a question regarding the 32 
defensible reason to allow this under those categories. The Committee was provided with 33 
information about the generator and any due diligence completed ahead of time, including how 34 
much it might cost and the project breakdown. Since that time, it became apparent that the hook 35 
up to the gas line from the street was referred to as low flow, however it is actually low pressure. 36 
The issue is that there is a 4” line coming in and it needs to be a 7” line. The Girdler House noted 37 
that a National Grid engineer had had reviewed this originally and signed off on it. It is unclear if 38 
someone actually visited the site or if someone from National Grid gave a verbal okay. It is 39 
unclear why National Grid would have said this was okay when it actually was not. The Girdler 40 
House sent the specs for the generator that they had installed, and it very clearly states on the 41 
specs that it requires a 7”-11” pipe. It is unclear why there was a disconnect between a 4” and 7” 42 
pipe. Also, in terms of the scope of work from the contractor they hired, there are not many 43 
specifics. It states that a 4” conduit will be installed from the transfer switch to the generator, but 44 
it is unclear if the contractor had a conversation with National Grid and was told that was okay, 45

or if the contractor simply looked at the size of the pipes and if they could align with the 46 
generator that was being installed. There are a lot of questions as to how the Girdler House ended 47 
up in this position and how there was such a miscommunication about how the generator would 48 
be connected. When the City does work with National Grid, there is a lot that goes into making 49 
sure that everything will align properly. It is surprising that the project got this far before a 50 
problem was noticed. Before the Committee decides whether they want to provide additional 51 
money to the Girdler House, there should be some due diligence done to determine if there is 52 
another source of funding for this project because it is a substantial amount. At the end of the 53 
day, this is the taxpayers’ money, right. It should be considered if there is another place for the 54 
Girdler House to turn for this money, not necessarily the CPC. 55 
 56 
Marino stated that it is unclear if the contractor from National Grid did its due diligence in the 57 
process. Oldmixon agreed that if there is a sign off somewhere from National Grid that makes 58 
this clear, then the Girdler House should be able to go back to National Grid regarding the costs. 59 
It is unclear how the initial sign off occurred. It appears that the same generator was installed as 60 
was originally considered, but she is unsure on this. Delios stated that she was told there was a 61 
site visit by National Grid with an electrician, but there was nothing formal and no follow up 62 
email to confirm this. Pearl asked if the plumbing quote was received and the Girdler House 63 
assumed the 4” pipe was fine.  64 
 65 
Pearl stated that the Girdler House could choose to submit a new application for the next cycle. 66 
Oldmixon stated that the Girdler House could also seek to amend its existing application, which 67 
it is trying to do in a way by requesting additional funds. Pearl stated that the Committee could 68 
determine an amendment to not be appropriate, and the Girdler House could still submit a new 69 
application in the next cycle. The Committee has to determine whether it believes the generator 70 
hookup can be sought under the category of preservation. Oldmixon stated that the Committee 71 
should make sure there is not another entity that the Girdler House should seek funding from for 72 
this project. It is worth checking with both the Girdler House and National Grid to obtain a 73 
record of who visited the site originally and what was discussed.  74 
 75 
Oldmixon stated that she believes the Girdler House could look to one of the other entities 76 
involved to help cover some of the delta of costs. It is unclear if the utility upgrade is only for the 77 
generator or the entire house. This may make a difference as to if it was a maintenance upgrade 78 
or just the generator. Pearl stated that, if the generator is determined to be the tool for 79 
preservation, then the upgrade to the generator would be okay to cover.  80 
 81 
The Committee agreed that it would generate a list of questions to pose to Girdler House. Pearl 82 
stated that the Girdler House mentioned that a licensed plumber pulled a pluming permit but 83 
there is no date listed. Oldmixon stated that she spoke with the Building Inspector who talked 84 
with the electrical inspector and it was relayed that generators are unique and they go by what 85 
the code says. Delios stated that the Girdler House says the generator was recommended by the 86 
generator company. Pearl asked about the Girdler House getting a smaller generator. Oldmixon 87 
noted that it could also be switched to diesel or propane which may not be very expensive, 88 
though then the fuel would need to be stored and there is not much space to do so. Pearl stated 89 
that, of the $77,000, $37,500 is for a booster pump, which is a material cost. The Committee 90
